rules.name: Optional - Prerequisite Calculus Courses
rules.desc: Students may need to complete the Math 19, 20 and 21 Calculus series as prerequisite courses for their ENVSE Minor coursework.
rules.notes: Many courses of interest require course Mechanics and/or course Linear Algebra, Multivariable Calculus, and Modern Applications as prerequisites.

rules.name: Requirements Guidelines
rules.desc:
Since undergraduates with varying backgrounds may be interested in obtaining an Environmental Systems Engineering minor, no single set of course requirements is appropriate for all students. Instead, interested students are encouraged to propose courses within the guidelines below.
General guidelines are:

• An Environmental Systems Engineering minor must contain at least 24 units of coursework not taken for the major and consist of at least six classes of at least three units each of letter-graded work, except where letter grades are not offered.

• The list of courses must represent a coherent body of knowledge in a focused area and should include classes that build upon one another.

• Two quarters prior to graduation, the student should meet with the Assistant Dir. of UG Degree Progress Rachel Stringari (rstring@stanford.edu) to review their course plan for graduation.

• Minors must be officially declared and all courses completed (or in progress) no later than the deadline for a student’s application to graduate.
Professor Peter Kitanidis (peterk@stanford.edu) is the CEE undergraduate minor advisor in Environmental Systems Engineering. Students must consult with Professor Kitanidis in developing their minor program and obtain his approval of the finalized study list on the CEE Environmental Systems Engineering Minor Program sheet and email to the CEE Assistant Director of Undergraduate Degree Progress.
